topicName: Build Tool Integration (Maven Surefire/Failsafe, Gradle Test Engine)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Build Tool Integration (Maven Surefire/Failsafe, Gradle Test Engine) in JUnit"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Integrating JUnit 5 with modern build tools is essential for automating test execution in Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines. This tutorial covers how to configure Apache Maven and Gradle to execute both unit tests and integration tests using the JUnit Platform."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. Maven Integration (Surefire and Failsafe Plugins)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Maven separates unit tests and integration tests using two distinct plugins: the Maven Surefire Plugin for unit tests and the Maven Failsafe Plugin for integration tests. Both require the JUnit Platform engine configuration."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Maven Surefire Plugin"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Surefire plugin runs during the test phase of the build lifecycle. To use JUnit 5, ensure you include the junit-jupiter dependency and configure the plugin version appropriately."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"<build>
    <plugins>
        <plugin>
            <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
            <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>3.2.5</version>
        </plugin>
    </plugins>
</build>"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Maven Failsafe Plugin for Integration Tests"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Integration tests typically run during the integration-test and verify phases. The Failsafe plugin ensures that integration tests run even if the build has failure conditions, but it ensures the build fails during verification if tests fail."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"<build>
    <plugins>
        <plugin>
            <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
            <artifactId>maven-failsafe-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>3.2.5</version>
            <executions>
                <execution>
                    <goals>
                        <goal>integration-test</goal>
                        <goal>verify</goal>
                    </goals>
                </execution>
            </executions>
        </plugin>
    </plugins>
</build>"},{"order":11,"type":"heading","text":"2. Gradle Integration (Gradle Test Engine)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Gradle has native support for JUnit 5 via the JUnit Platform. You do not need separate plugins for unit and integration tests unless you are setting up custom source sets."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring build.gradle"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"To enable JUnit 5 in Gradle, apply the standard test task configuration using useJUnitPlatform()."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"plugins {
    id 'java'
}

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    testImplementation platform('org.junit:junit-bom:5.10.2')
    testImplementation 'org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter'
}

test {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    testLogging {
        events "passed", "skipped", "failed"
    }
}"},{"order":16,"type":"heading","text":"3. Advanced Configuration and Filtering"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Both build tools allow advanced filtering of tests using Tags or Test Engines. This is particularly useful for separating fast unit tests from slow integration tests."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Filtering by Tags in Maven Surefire"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"<plugin>
    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
    <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>3.2.5</version>
    <configuration>
        <excludedGroups>integration</excludedGroups>
    </configuration>
</plugin>"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Filtering by Tags in Gradle"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"test {
    useJUnitPlatform {
        includeTags 'fast'
        excludeTags 'slow'
    }
}"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always use a Bill of Materials (BOM) like junit-bom to manage transitive JUnit dependency versions consistently."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Maven Surefire for unit tests (*Test.java) and Failsafe for integration tests (*IT.java)."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ensure useJUnitPlatform() is explicitly called in Gradle configurations; otherwise, Gradle will default to JUnit 4."}]
